Summary Description: Xiangming Xiao conducts interdisciplinary geospatial and environmental science research, bridging urban climatology, remote sensing, and sustainable land-use planning. His work emphasizes explainable machine learning approaches to quantify how urban form, greenspace, and landscape structure drive microclimates at fine scales, supporting scalable, LCZ-informed urban planning for climate resilience. He also contributes to high-resolution, morphology-based oil palm mapping using sub-meter RGB imagery, providing global-scale data products for forestry and agricultural management with minimal reliance on training data. Together, his research advances reproducible, interpretable analytics that inform urban design, land-use policy, and environmental stewardship across rapidly changing urban and agricultural landscapes.
